messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: p99 latency breach detected for customer AstraNova (VPC eu-west-1) against dedicated pool 'dn-az-3'. Alert: p99 > 4s for the last 5m. Paging on-call.
leah_oncall: on it. pulling metrics. can someone confirm impacted endpoints? /gen and /chat are showing surges.
omar_sre: confirmed p95 and p99 spike on gen endpoints, seq len distribution shifted up (avg tokens/request ~ 2.5x). KV cache resident size for pool spiked, lots of shard imbalance. logs: "kv_cache_eviction_rate=high" and increased tail latency on CPU-side batching.
julia_acct: looped in customer success (AstraNova). they report some production invoices stalled and user-facing timeouts. asking for ETA.
leah_oncall: initial mitigation: isolate AstraNova traffic from noisy tenant routing? it's already in dedicated pool but we can pin them to a warm spare node group while we investigate.
max_se: quick note — customer uses long-context prompts with per-request system instructions and dynamic tool outputs, probably causing few supersessions to fill KV cache. recommend prefix-trimming and session TTL enforcement.
yan_runtime: can we route AstraNova to a quantized model variant (gpt-small-q) temporarily? capacity available in eu-west warm pool. tradeoff: slight quality drop but should cut per-token CPU by ~30%.
omar_sre: moving traffic to warm spare now. running graceful drain on primary nodes to reduce KV churn. applying temporary rate-limit to 120 rps for tertiary endpoints. also enabling aggressive KV eviction policy (ttl=60s) for that pool.
ops-bot: deploy-note: traffic-shift job started by leah_oncall at 2026-03-17T10:05:12Z — job id shift-176888A
leah_oncall: @ryan_runtime please kick the fallback model route and confirm latency delta. @omar_sre keep an eye on retry storm.
ryan_runtime: routing rule applied: AstraNova -> gpt-small-q (compat mode) for /gen endpoints. initial p99 dropped from ~4.8s -> 1.3s for sampled requests. p95 now ~600ms.
julia_acct: relaying to customer: "we've shifted you to a temporary lower-latency model and throttled burst traffic to stabilize. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline for full restoration." they asked for window and rollback plan.
omar_sre: rollback plan: when KV churn reduces and primary nodes show stable resident cache <70% for 10min, we'll move back in 5-min canary increments. expecting 30-45m.
max_se: proposing long-term fixes: session-based prefix dedupe, enforce max prompt token limit per tenant, and introduce per-tenant KV compaction task. filing follow-up RFC.
leah_oncall: tagging incident type: customer-impacting, dedicated-pool, KV-cache. creating post-incident follow-up ticket and scheduling bridge with runtime team + SE.
ops-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-176888-ASTRA — severity: P1 — owner: leah_oncall
omar_sre: noticed a small retry surge 2m after shift due to client-side retry logic — added 429 instead of queuing to upstream. reduced retry amplification.
ryan_runtime: added temporary batching cap: max_batch_tokens_per_request lowered to 4096 for that pool to prevent oversized batches causing sequencing delays.
julia_acct: customer acknowledges stabilization but requests detailed timeline and indemnity for SLA window. I'll open an account-level follow-up and coordinate legal if needed.
leah_oncall: handing off to on-call lead for extended remediation and root-cause analysis. @omar_sre you'll lead RCA, @ryan_runtime you'll own model routing playbook, @max_se you'll own customer-facing engineering summary.
omar_sre: accepted handoff. capturing logs, perf traces, and KV metrics. will run heap-profiling on runtime nodes during next warm maintenance window.
leah_oncall: thanks team. final status: customer stabilized on fallback model, p99 within SLO for last 3m. moving thread to incident postmortem channel in 30m for docs. :white_check_mark:
